analysis: The supplied units are head-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 36292-37818): test-vector data only (token ID arrays, a 'long_prompt' vector with repeated 'cache' text, a plan with prompt_contract_id, prompt_token_count 1025, block_boundaries and chain_hash values for 256/512/768/1024 tokens, and fixed _darkbloom_prompt_date 2028-02-29). The patch excerpt shows another vector gaining additional_context {enable_thinking:false}, with token counts and chain hashes regenerated (803 to 767 tokens, 3 blocks to 2). This is consistent with regenerated golden vectors for the prompt-contract/prefix-cache keying (relevant to T-041). There is no executable code, auth logic, key material, secrets or network behavior in the changed ranges. The fixtures contain no real user data (synthetic 'cache' repetition). Security-relevant questions that remain outside the supplied evidence: (1) whether the Swift provider and Go/coordinator code that consume these vectors actually implement the new enable_thinking/additional_context normalization consistently, so that prompt_contract_id and chain_hash keying (cache scoping across tenants, T-041/A-001) are not weakened; (2) whether the scope_id 'fixture-scope' semantics match production scoping. The patch is truncated and the source changes that would motivate the vector change were not supplied, so I cannot confirm that scope/tenant separation is still bound into the chain hashes. No concrete regression is identified from fixture data alone.
